label: Jumia
terms_note: Jumia vendor (Mastershop) account; the vendor registers an application in Vendor Center (type Self Authorization or Web Application — cannot be changed later); OAuth2 Bearer tokens via /login and /token; rate limit 200 requests / minute and 4 requests / second per Mastershop; no sandbox; multi-country (CI, DZ, EG, GH, KE, MA, NG, SN, TN, UG, ZA).

discovery.auth: oauth2 (application registered in Vendor Center › Settings › Applications; Self-Authorization refresh_token grant for unattended ERPs, or Web Application authorization_code; Bearer access token)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Vendor Center › Settings › Applications → register an app; choose Self Authorization (refresh_token grant, unattended) or Web Application (authorization_code).
2. Obtain tokens via `/login` and `/token`; refresh with the refresh_token grant.

endpoints.notes: feed statuses PENDING / IN_PROGRESS / COMPLETED / FAILED

endpoints.purpose: read products (status, QC, visibility filters) + reference data
pack with tracking code, ready to ship, label

reference.limits: 200 requests / minute with a ceiling of 4 requests / second, per Mastershop. - Vendor agreement per Jumia country; the app type is fixed at creation. - No sandbox — test carefully on live data.
mcp_sdk: none official found in the pages opened

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: Client Id of a SELF AUTHORIZATION application registered in Vendor Center > Settings > Applications (Web Applications cannot refresh unattended).

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Refresh token from the application's 'Generate Token' action in Vendor Center. Every refresh returns a NEW refresh token; the runtime keeps it in memory and, with PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR set, saves it to <dir>/jumia.json (0600) so a restart uses the latest one.

adapter.terms: Jumia Vendor API (Africa: NG, EG, KE, MA, CI, GH, SN, TN, UG, DZ, ZA). Product feeds are asynchronous (201 with a feedId; see GET /feeds/{id}). Order roles VC - Order Viewer / Order Manager are required. This adapter targets the live host (vendor-api.jumia.com); the staging host is not selectable because the token URL is fixed.

me.note: get-shops returns the shops of the authenticated user [{id, name, email, businessClients[{code (e.g. jumia-ng), countryCode, status}]}].

set_inventory.note: Update Product Stock feed {products: [{sellerSku, id, stock}]}: BOTH `sku` (your seller SKU) and `listing_id` (the Jumia product SID, a uuid) are required by the endpoint. Asynchronous: raw.feedId, status at GET /feeds/{id}.

list_orders.note: Retrieve Orders ?status(PENDING|READY_TO_SHIP|SHIPPED|DELIVERED|FAILED|CANCELED|RETURNED, comma-separated)&createdAfter(YYYY-MM-DD or 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss'; createdBefore defaults to today, max 3-month window)&size. Paging is by the response's next-page token, so only the first page is returned. raw.number is the customer-facing order number; totals are in the local currency.

not_offered.create_listing: Product creation goes through the /feeds/products/create feed with category, brand, attribute set and variation data; the vocabulary has no category or brand.
not_offered.update_listing: The price feed POST /feeds/products/price requires id (product SID), sellerSku AND price for every product; update_listing has no SKU input, so the required sellerSku cannot be supplied.
not_offered.end_listing: Status changes use the /feeds/products/status feed, which requires id, sellerSku and per-country businessClients[{businessClientCode, status}]; end_listing carries neither the SKU nor the business client.
not_offered.mark_shipped: Shipping is item-based: POST /orders/pack and /orders/ready-to-ship take orderItemIds (and shipment provider / tracking per package), not an order id.
